description: S328 merge-blocker. A `:`-shorthand per-item body (§4.14) whose expression CALLS a same-file MIXED-return fn (markup on one path, a plain string on the other) inside an RCDATA parent (<textarea>). The markup-capable analysis is a MAY-analysis, so the call is treated as markup-yielding even when it returns a string — but a <textarea>'s value IS its child TEXT content, so mounting a `<span data-scrml-mv>` there makes `textarea.value` read "" and the adopter's string is gone. Pins: ZERO element children inside the textarea.
rationale: SPEC §4.14 line 1021: 'a `:`-shorthand body IS the element's single-expression body, byte-identical to the bare-body form `<tag>${expr}</tag>`' — carried into <each> scope verbatim by §17.7.6 ('No `<each>`-specific extension to the `§4.14` grammar is introduced'). The bare-body form already lowers an RCDATA body to `.value`; the shorthand form must do the same. Pre-fix (S327/#456) the shorthand branch had no content-model guard and appended a `<span data-scrml-mv>` INSIDE the <textarea>. ASSERTION NOTE, load-bearing: this harness runs on happy-dom, and happy-dom is NOT a valid oracle for either half of this defect — MEASURED, its `textarea.value` getter falls back to `textContent` and returns "alpha" for BOTH the buggy span-mount and the correct `.value` write. A `value:` assertion CANNOT discriminate this. The gate is therefore the DOM-SHAPE counts: `textarea *` and `textarea [data-scrml-mv]` are 0 only when no element child was injected. The `value:` row is corroboration for a conformant-DOM impl, not the gate. RCDATA is the ONLY content model this refusal covers — see each-shorthand-option-label-preserved for why widening it to <option> was measured to be a regression.
